newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Court confirms jail for S.Korea's Roh, Chun.
newsitem.headline: Court confirms jail for S.Korea's Roh, Chun.

text.p: South Korea's Supreme Court on Thursday rejected prosecution appeals against reduced sentences for former presidents Chun Doo Hwan and Roh Tae-woo for their roles in a coup and an army massacre.
It upheld a lower appeals court decision in December to commute Chun's death sentence to life in jail and Roh's 22-1/2 year prison term to 17 years for mutiny and treason.

The charges relate to a 1979 coup that thrust then army general Chun to power and a massacre in 1980 in the southwestern city of Kwangju that crushed democratic opposition and left deep scars on the nation.
Both ex-presidents were also convicted in last year's "trial of the century" of amassing hundreds of millions of dollars in slush funds from businessmen while in office.
Chun was fined 220.5 billion won ($247 million) and Roh 262.8 billion.
A panel of judges in the highest appeals court in the land also upheld sentences on 12 former generals for their roles in the putsch and army killings.

They also confirmed suspended jail sentences on two tycoons, including the chairmen of the giant Daewoo and Dong Ah Groups, and the acquittal of two others, including Chung Tae-soo, founder of the Hanbo Group.
Chung is on trial in a separate bribery case involving the collapse of Hanbo's steelmaking flagship.
Some of the nation's top moguls were convicted of bribing Roh and Chun to obtain business favours.
A Supreme Court statement said the lower court's verdicts could not be overturned because they contained no constitutional flaws.
President Kim Young-sam is widely expected to offer his predecessors a pardon before he steps down from office next February.
"We cannot confirm or deny the media reports," said a Blue House official, referring to newspaper articles in the past week speculating about a date for an amnesty.
Some reports said an amnesty could come as early as May 14, Buddha's birthday.
Families of the Kwangju massacre victims and human rights groups are fighting to keep Chun and Roh in jail.

"We are outraged that talk of granting clemency to murderous suspects of treason should have surfaced from the ruling New Korea Party even before the final ruling," said a statement by Minkahyup, a rights group.
Chun was president from 1980-1988 and Roh succeeded him, stepping down in 1993.
The 12 generals were jailed for between 3-1/2 years and eight years. Another convicted ex-general died this month.
Daewoo founder Kim Woo-choong's two-year suspended jail term was upheld along with a 2-1/2 year suspended sentence for Choi Won-suk, chairman of the Dong Ah Group.
The court also confirmed the acquittal of Lee Kyung-hoon, former president of Daewoo Corp, Daewoo Group's trading arm.

Chun's death sentence was commuted by the Seoul High Court in recognition of his role in the fast-paced economic development of the Asian "Tiger" and the peaceful transfer of the presidency to Roh in 1988.
Chun and Roh defended their 1979 military takeover as needed to quell civil insurrection that they said threatened to expose South Korea to attack from the communist North. (Conversion: $1 = 894 won)
